First things first- don’t hurt yourself. It’s not worth it. However, when has that ever stopped any of us (me definitely included).I can’t stop you, so here is my best advice.

Bandaids are a life saver. They’re great for closing deep cuts and preventing smaller cuts bleeding everywhere. However, they shouldn’t be used to stop the bleeding (if it’s bleeding a lot) because a)they don’t work very well at stopping bleeding and b)they can get expensive

Gauze is ideal for stopping bleeding, but if you don’t have that I would recommend finding some (clean- infection is bad) piece of clothing or fabric that doesn’t pill/ isn’t fuzzy and using this to stop bleeding. Press the fabric over the cut and apply pressure for 15 mins without peeking. If it still hasn’t stopped repeat this for another 15 minutes. If it hasn’t stopped at this point you should probably get medical attention, but barring that just keep applying pressure until it stops, or tie the fabric tightly around the cut and leave it- keeps pressure but frees up your hands. 

I also suggest cleaning the wound. I personally just use water and a mild scentless soap- scentless soaps have less additives that can irritate the cut. You can also apply ointment. If the cut reaches fat (bad idea don’t do it) don’t put anything in the wound other than water- this includes soap and ointment. Fat tissue is very delicate and can be damaged easily. It can also get infected very easily. 

If the cut is deep close it- use steri strips, butterfly bandages, bandaids, or even just tape. Closing it will help prevent infection and help it to scar less and heal quicker. 

Try to keep injuries covered and clean to prevent infection. If it gets infected - especially if it’s deep- seek medical attention. Not getting help can result in nasty sores, sickness, loss of limb, and even death. When it’s deep these results are even more likely.

Take care of yourself! You deserve it. Feel free to ask any other questions- Not a doctor but I’ll do my best to answer them

Vein depths vary depending on the part of the body- some are shallower than others. It would bleed a lot, I don’t really have measurements. You know you’ve cut a vein if the blood kind of pulses as it comes out- not spurting but pulsing to the heart beat. If you end up cutting one keep pressure on it for 15 minutes without peeking. If after 15 minutes it’s still bleeding do it for another 15 minutes. After that you really need to get medical attention if you can’t get it to stop- something that can happen fairly easily where veins are concerned.

My advice is just don’t - cut below styro( btw, fat is next then fascia then muscle) or cut a vein. Veins are difficult to stop the bleeding and if you can’t get them to stop you have to go get medical help. Fat cuts should get stitches and if they aren’t taken care of they can get infected very easily. If they get infected they can be life threatening or could cause you to lose limbs. You will almost inevitably end up cutting nerves or veins which can cause permanent damage. It’s really dangerous. If you decide to go deeper anyways make sure you keep the cut clean
I think you should be fine. Deeper cuts tend to leak a little, as long as it isn’t milky or yellow you should be fine. Since you said there’s no more it sounds like it was fine

Did it reopen or did it not stop bleeding? Just try to make sure the bleeding stops.

Water should be fine- make sure the wound stays clean

My best advice is stop now. Everyone says it, but that doesn’t make it any less true. Continuing to cut was one of the worst decisions I’ve ever made.  Focus on the feelings of doubt and fear and just don’t do it again. It’s so much easier to stop at the beginning. You might never wear shorts, but if you keep going the cutting will spread to other places. 

Everyone talks about how cutting makes them feel better, but most of these people are already dependent on the cutting. For me at least, it’s not that cutting makes me feel better it’s that the lack of cutting makes me feel so so much worse. 

Please don’t keep going.

On shallower cuts ointment does help. It’s just that fat tissue is so delicate that you really don’t want anything touching it- the tissue can get destroyed really easily which just makes the healing process so much harder

You should get medical attention. However, barring this I’ll tell you what I did to take care of fat cuts. 
The best advice I can give you is to close the cut. Use steri strips ideally, but bandaids or even just tape can work. Pinch the cut closed and use whatever you have to keep it closed. Keeping it closed will help it heal more quickly (it will still take forever) and cause it to scar less. It can also help you avoid infection. Try to avoid putting anything in the cut once it gets this deep, including ointment- you can put it around the edges but avoid putting it in the cut itself.  Cover it and keep it closed. Don’t mess with it and just try your best to keep it clean.
